newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turk far-right party says not joining new govt.
newsitem.headline: Turk far-right party says not joining new govt.

text.p: A key Turkish far-right party said on Monday it would not join a caretaker government sought by the crumbling Islamist-led coalition, jeopardising the alliance's plans for early elections.
"We have broken off the talks which we have held until now. There is no question of the BBP...joining the government," Grand Unity Party (BBP) deputy chairman Mehmet Ekici told reporters.
The government was relying on the BBP's support to get planned snap polls through parliament, which must pass legislation in support of new elections.
Islamist Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan and his conservative partner Tansu Ciller announced on June 1 that they were seeking early elections. No date for the polls has been set.
The government's ability to win parliamentary support for the polls has been weakened by the erosion of its majority in parliament after a series of resignations from Ciller's True Path Party.
Erbakan's coalition had sought the elections to clear up a festering row with the secularist establishment over army-led demands for a crackdown on Islamist activism.
